column3: The Hebrew has “spoke” and “saying,” without an explicit “Again”; BSB adds “Again” and omits a separate saying expression.
The Hebrew repeats the giving instruction and “to the Levites” for cities and pastureland; BSB combines them into one giving instruction.

The Hebrew repeats “cubits” with each of the four measurements and has no explicit “larger” for the pasturelands; BSB gives the unit once and adds “larger.”

The Hebrew ends with each person giving from “his cities,” without explicitly naming a tribe; BSB expresses the allocation by “each tribe.”
The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB condenses these to “said.”

The Hebrew repeats the giving verb and “the three cities”; BSB gives one selecting command for both groups.
The Hebrew joins the resident foreigner and sojourner with “and”; BSB uses “or” between “foreigner” and “stranger.”
The Hebrew separates the attacker’s striking from the victim’s dying; BSB makes the attacker the subject of both “strikes” and “kills.”
The Hebrew says a stone “by which he may die,” without explicitly describing its size; BSB specifies “a stone of deadly size.”
The Hebrew separates the attacker’s striking from the victim’s dying; BSB makes the attacker the subject of “strikes and kills.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the thrown object unnamed and separately says the victim dies; BSB supplies “an object” and makes the attacker the subject of “kills him.”

The Hebrew says a stone “by which he may die,” without an explicit weight adjective; BSB calls it “a heavy stone.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses active singular “he anointed him” for the high priest; BSB uses passive “who was anointed.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “the avenger of blood” and says “he has no blood”; BSB replaces the repeated title with pronouns and explains the phrase as not being guilty of bloodshed.
The Hebrew repeats “the manslayer” in the returning clause; BSB uses “he” and adds “Only” before “after the death.”
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew uses an active killing verb and prohibits a lone witness from testifying to a person’s death; BSB uses passive “be put to death” and expresses the latter prohibition as a restriction on execution based on one witness.
